query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermomechanical processing via cold rolling with a 20–40% reduction followed by annealing at 850 K for 1 hour will refine the grain structure of MnNiSi, thereby enhancing mechanical performance while maintaining a large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk MnNiSi alloy with a coarse grain structure and inherent microstructural defects that limit mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Apply cold rolling with a reduction of 20–40% to introduce plastic deformation, then perform an annealing treatment at 850 K for 1 hour under inert conditions.
generation.conditions: Conduct processing in an inert atmosphere to avoid oxidation, ensuring that the annealing temperature is controlled to favor recrystallization and grain refinement without triggering unwanted phase transformations.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined, homogeneous grain structure with a reduced density of internal defects.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement leads to improved yield strength and toughness by increasing grain boundary area, which impedes dislocation motion while preserving the microstructural features crucial for a robust magnetocaloric transition.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy will exhibit increased yield strength and ductility while retaining a high magnetic entropy change similar to that of the as-synthesized state.
generation.baseline: MnNiSi in its as-synthesized, coarse-grained state has a strong magnetocaloric effect but poor mechanical integrity.
generation.boundary: Excessive deformation or an annealing temperature that is too high could lead to grain overgrowth or phase changes that might compromise the magnetocaloric properties.
generation.uncertainty: While the proposed processing window (20–40% cold rolling and 850 K annealing) is based on typical values for similar systems, the exact optimum requires experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Subject a set of MnNiSi samples to 20–40% cold rolling followed by annealing at 850 K for 1 hour. Characterize the grain size distribution by electron microscopy, test mechanical properties via tensile testing, and measure the magnetocaloric effect (ΔS) as a function of temperature.
measurements: Electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) for grain size and boundary analysis
Tensile tests for mechanical strength and ductility
Magnetization measurements for determining the peak magnetocaloric entropy change
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples fail to display improved mechanical properties or suffer a significant (>15%) reduction in ΔS compared to the baseline, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: However, the mechanical properties have only been reported for as-recrystallized Co-rich HEAs. The microstructure has a strong correlation with the mechanical properties of metals and alloys, which are usually tuned by thermomechanical processing (TMP), such as rolling, compression, and torsion, combined with heat-treatment [,,,,,,,,,]. The influence of TMP on the resultant microstructure and the correlation between the microstructure and mechanical performance of the newly developed Co-rich HEAs have not yet been revealed. The regulation of the microstructure is a prerequisite for optimizing the mechanical performance of metals and alloys; thus, gaining a deep understanding of microstructure optimization and its influence on their mechanical properties is crucial. These will become guidelines for fabricating high-performance materials that deserve in-depth investigation. In this study, we aimed to clarify the effect of TMP on the microstructure and room-temperature tensile properties of Co-rich Co35Cr25Ni15Mn15Fe10 (at%) TRIP-HEA. The results demonstrated that the TMP-induced grain refinement contributed significantly to enhancing the tensile strength while retaining good ductilit

In the present study, we succeeded in tuning the microstructure and improving the room-temperature tensile properties of a high-performance Co-rich Co35Cr25Ni15Mn15Fe10 (at%) TRIP-HEA, achieved by using thermomechanical processings of rolling and heat-treatment. The correlation between the microstructures and the strengthening mechanism of the samples at each stage was clarified. The grains were non-uniformly refined by the hot-rolling process but were significantly refined and homogenized after cold-rolling, followed by appropriate heat treatment. The grain size was refined from 144.4 μm to 1.83 μm by cold-rolling and subsequent annealing at 973 K; meanwhile, the Cr-rich σ-phase with a volume fraction of 0.413% and an average size of 118.8 nm was formed. It was found that grain refinement is the most effective method for enhancing the tensile strength while retaining ductility, whereas the formation of incoherent precipitates slightly improves strength but sacrifices ductility.
